2.6 Exercises

Exercise 2.6.1. Let \(C_0\) and \(C_1\) be categories and consider morphisms \(f_0\colon x_0 \to y_0\) and \(g_0\colon y_0 \to z_0\) in \(C_0\) and morphisms \(f_1\colon x_1 \to y_1\) and \(g_1\colon y_1 \to z_1\) in \(C_1\). Show that the composite \((g_0,g_1) \circ (f_0,f_1)\colon (x_0,x_1) \to (z_0,z_1)\) in \(C_0 \times C_1\) is given by \((g_0 \circ f_0, g_1 \circ f_1)\).

Agda Composition in a product

product-composition

Derivation, checked

product-composition : {Γ C D : CAT} {x₁ y₁ z₁ : MAP Γ C} {x₂ y₂ z₂ : MAP Γ D}
  (f₁ : MorphismExpression x₁ y₁) (g₁ : MorphismExpression y₁ z₁)
  (f₂ : MorphismExpression x₂ y₂) (g₂ : MorphismExpression y₂ z₂) →
  ExpressionIso (compose-expression (pair-expression f₁ f₂) (pair-expression g₁ g₂))
    (pair-expression (compose-expression f₁ g₁) (compose-expression f₂ g₂))
Proof / implementation
product-composition = At.comparison

About this correspondence

The proof applies to absolute morphisms and tests composition on hom categories. Neither Rezk nor recognition is a parameter.
